body:
PR-1998 REBASED AND PUSHED — a2d401e3c2. CONFLICTING/DIRTY -> MERGEABLE. It was
43 behind; it is now 0.

THE CONFLICT AND WHICH SIDE SURVIVED. One file, watch.rs, one hunk, and it was a
both-sides case rather than a pick-one:

    main        EventKind::QueueDrained { shipped, shelved, excluded_from_batch, ineligible }
                — TASK-1297 added two fields
    the branch  adds two NEW arms, SpecCompleted and RunCompleted,
                and still carried the old 2-field QueueDrained

So neither side was discardable: the branch's whole point is the two new arms,
and main's QueueDrained signature is the current one. Resolved as the branch's
two new arms followed by MAIN's 4-field pattern. The shared body below the hunk
already referenced `ineligible` and `excluded_from_batch`, which is what
confirms main's signature is the one it belongs to.

VERIFIED, not assumed:
    markers on the COMMITTED tree      0
    all three arms present in watch.rs SpecCompleted 1, RunCompleted 1, QueueDrained 5
    aida-cli-lib --lib                 5200 passed, 0 failed

The compile is the real proof on the pattern question: with the 4-field enum,
any surviving 2-field pattern is a type error, so a clean build means none
survived. I checked the arms by grep as well rather than relying on that alone.

STATE: mergeable=MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED — the hold is still on it
and its verdict is CHANGES REQUESTED with NO SHA, one of BUG-1466's five. So it
is now REVIEWABLE, which is what you asked for, but under your amended criterion
4 it cannot be released by a stale verdict — it needs a fresh one carrying a sha.
Flagging so the reviewer is not sent to re-read a verdict that cannot clear it.

I have not touched the hold. I wrote the commit.

ON #2042: taken, and I was wrong to list it as an anomaly. A trailer hazard hold
standing WITHOUT a verdict is correct, not a gap — the absent verdict file is
the right state for a hold that is not a refusal. I will stop reporting it, and
the distinction is worth having in BUG-1532's kind taxonomy: your criterion 1
splits SUPERVISED from REFUSAL, and this is a third thing — a hold that no
review can clear because what it is waiting on is a trailer resolution, not a
verdict.

NEXT: say the word. Not starting anything without a start-ack.
subject: PR-1998 MERGEABLE (a2d401e3c2) — both-sides conflict resolved, 5200/0; but its verdict has no sha so criterion 4 blocks release
